scope: Professional procedural terrain architecture, mathematics, ancient paleohydrology, dry landscape processes, streaming, materials and bounded non-heightfield features

sources.title: Landscape Technical Guide
sources.finding: Landscape components are rendering, visibility and collision units; sections are LOD units; shared border vertices are duplicated; component and section counts have CPU and draw-call costs.
sources.decision: Adopt explicit source-tile, render-patch and border contracts; do not copy Unreal dimensions or limits.

sources.title: World Partition
sources.finding: A persistent world is subdivided into grid cells and loaded around streaming sources; HLOD and data layers are adjacent systems.
sources.decision: Keep identity, storage, derived products and active residency separate; retain multi-anchor priority in RegionStream.

sources.title: Procedural Content Generation Framework
sources.finding: Production procedural workflows combine spatial data, attributes, interactivity, extensibility and traditional authored content from utilities through whole worlds.
sources.decision: Use a versioned engine-owned stage graph and authored constraints; do not build a visual node editor now.

sources.title: Landscape Materials
sources.finding: Landscape material layers are driven by weight data and support weighted, alpha and height-aware blending.
sources.decision: Cook normalized physical base weights and separate additive overlays; support height-aware contacts.

sources.title: Using Nanite with Landscapes
sources.finding: Nanite terrain can improve rendering but retains the non-Nanite landscape for other systems, adds data residency and rebuild requirements, and uses skirts for seams.
sources.decision: Do not clone Nanite. Measure our tiled hierarchy first and preserve derived-cache rebuild boundaries.

sources.title: TerrainData
sources.finding: Terrain source data separates heightmaps, alpha maps, holes, detail patches and far basemaps; patch maximum-height-error data is exposed.
sources.decision: Separate canonical fields from derived meshes/material composites and store geometric-error metadata.

sources.title: Terrain settings reference
sources.finding: Terrain exposes instancing, pixel-error simplification, complexity bounds and a low-resolution composite beyond the basemap distance.
sources.decision: Use projected geometric error, shared instances and a far material composite.

sources.title: Terrain.SetNeighbors
sources.finding: Explicit neighbor connections let adjacent tiles coordinate LOD.
sources.decision: Make tile adjacency and border revision explicit rather than inferring it in rendering.

sources.title: Terrain Tools: Erosion
sources.finding: The tools distinguish hydraulic, thermal and wind erosion, and erosion detail depends on sample resolution.
sources.decision: Use hydraulic/fluvial methods only to reconstruct ancient formation, then stop liquid processes and run distinct dry talus and aeolian stages.

sources.title: Improving Noise and reference implementation
sources.finding: Improved gradient noise corrects interpolation discontinuity and gradient issues in the original algorithm and provides a stable reference implementation.
sources.decision: Use a deterministic coherent noise basis only as a band-limited scaffold and version its algorithm.

sources.title: A Survey of Procedural Noise Functions
sources.finding: Noise families have different spectral, anisotropy, performance and filtering properties; there is no universal best noise.
sources.decision: Select noise per field and validate spectra/aliasing instead of accumulating fashionable noise types.

sources.title: Terrain Generation Using Procedural Models Based on Hydrology
sources.finding: A drainage graph, watersheds, river characterization and procedural patches can generate controllable continuous terrain from a compact sketch.
sources.decision: Make fossil drainage topology and guide constraints earlier than detailed height synthesis; publish no present-day water state.

sources.title: Priority-Flood: An Optimal Depression-Filling and Watershed-Labeling Algorithm for Digital Elevation Models
sources.finding: Priority-Flood provides a general depression-filling basis and can support flow direction and watershed labeling on regular or irregular terrain.
sources.decision: Prototype it for ancient drainage reconstruction and unwanted-pit resolution while retaining explicitly authored fossil closed basins.

sources.title: D-Infinity Flow Directions
sources.finding: D-infinity derives continuous flow direction from the steepest triangular facet and apportions flow between two neighbors.
sources.decision: Prototype ancient flow reconstruction against simpler D8 and retain deterministic flat/tie rules; do not use it as current water simulation.

sources.title: Physically-based analytical erosion for fast terrain generation
sources.finding: Analytical stream-power solutions with multigrid acceleration can bridge fast procedural control and physically grounded large-scale erosion, including hillslopes and landslides.
sources.decision: Evaluate as an offline ancient-formation pass before committing to costly droplet or long iterative erosion; follow with a separate dry-age pass.

sources.title: Efficient Debris-flow Simulation for Steep Terrain Erosion
sources.finding: Debris flow complements fluvial erosion on steep, low-drainage terrain where simple slope-reducing erosion becomes unrealistically uniform.
sources.decision: Represent present dry talus/rockfall separately from any ancient wet debris history; preserve full simulation as a later authoring cook.

sources.title: Windblown sand around obstacles - simulation and validation of deposition patterns
sources.finding: Wind flow, saltation and avalanching reproduce characteristic sand deposition around obstacles and include qualitative validation and source code.
sources.decision: Use a separate present-day mobile-sand field and prototype detailed dry deposition only in bounded zones.

sources.title: A Review of Digital Terrain Modeling
sources.finding: Heightfields are efficient but cannot represent caves and overhangs; volumetric methods enable them at higher cost; erosion, feature and example-based approaches have complementary strengths.
sources.decision: Use a heightfield plus sparse feature surfaces rather than one representation for every landform.

sources.title: Table Mountains by Virtual Erosion
sources.finding: Separate resistant rock and eroded soft material layers plus thermal erosion can form rimrock and talus characteristic of mesas.
sources.decision: Store bedrock/lithology separately from sediment and use hardness-dependent erosion.

sources.title: Arenite: A Physics-based Sandstone Simulator
sources.finding: Layer hardness, stress, wind/fluvial erosion and deposition can generate sandstone arches, alcoves, hoodoos and buttes under user control.
sources.decision: Treat as a future bounded feature-authoring technique, not the initial world generator.

sources.title: Geometry Clipmaps: Terrain Rendering Using Nested Regular Grids
sources.finding: Nested viewer-centered regular grids support incremental refill, on-demand synthesis and bounded terrain rendering cost.
sources.decision: Retain as a later rendering candidate after a measured tiled/error-LOD baseline.

sources.title: Smooth View-Dependent Level-of-Detail Control and its Application to Terrain Rendering
sources.finding: Screen-space error, block hierarchies and runtime geomorphs provide spatially and temporally continuous terrain LOD without visible popping.
sources.decision: Replace fixed-distance LOD with error metadata, hysteresis and geomorphing.

sources.title: Generating Complex Procedural Terrains Using the GPU
sources.finding: 3D density fields and Marching Cubes represent caves and overhangs in generated blocks, but introduce block scheduling, LOD transition and texturing problems.
sources.decision: Use density fields only for bounded features and measure CPU/GPU ownership before selecting a backend.

sources.title: Dual Contouring of Hermite Data
sources.finding: Hermite intersection and normal data plus quadratic error functions can preserve sharp features while contouring and simplifying adaptive grids.
sources.decision: Compare with Marching Cubes on one layered canyon/overhang fixture before adoption.

sources.title: The Transvoxel Algorithm for Voxel Terrain
sources.finding: Transition cells stitch Marching-Cubes-style voxel meshes across exact 2:1 resolution boundaries.
sources.decision: Preserve as a later option only if bounded volumetric feature cells require multiresolution streaming.

sources.title: Fast Poisson Disk Sampling in Arbitrary Dimensions
sources.finding: A background grid and bounded candidate attempts generate efficient blue-noise point distributions.
sources.decision: Use as a placement prototype only with world-stable candidate identities and cross-tile ownership.
